title: TTRPG Historical Continuation: World and Story

sections.title: Two Aza’ra Campaign Eras
sections.text:
The tabletop game supports a historical Belavadös setting and a distinct Galaxy Era around 3013 CE in an alternate continuity.
Campaign creation requires an era selection because available places, transport, knowledge and technology are not interchangeable.
A story in the later era must not send adventurers to the destroyed continent as though it still exists.
The tabletop rules can share mechanics across eras while changing available equipment, communication and hazards.
Historical and system reference
The historical and Galaxy Era settings share their core resolution logic but must not share maps, technology lists or historical knowledge without explanation. The alternate Galaxy Era around 3013 CE is not Pix's 2036 present. The original two-era constraint belongs in every saved campaign state.
Next chapter

sections.title: Belavadös Before Destruction
sections.text:
Most historical tabletop campaigns center on Belavadös before the Iron Dominion destroys it.
Characters can encounter its ports, polities and oral traditions while those communities are still living.
Later documents may describe ruins or migration, but cannot treat the original continent as surviving terrain.
The destruction is attributed to the Iron Dominion, not Tzaphaer.
Keep the historical date of the bombing unresolved until a dated canonical source establishes it.
Next chapter

sections.title: The Cataclysm of 1351 BCE
sections.text:
Uxrowo’s cataclysm and language convergence occur in 1351 BCE.
This event begins Aza’ra’s reconstructed civilization and involves a planetary catastrophe, surviving Uxrowoiye psionics and Kaʻaheʻanua magic.
The Iron Dominion’s later destruction of Belavadös is tracked separately.
Players in an era close to the catastrophe should face broken geography and unstable infrastructure, not modern Moonpunk installations.
Next chapter

sections.title: Galaxy Era, Around 3013 CE
sections.text:
The Galaxy Era is an alternate-universe spacefaring campaign option.
It centers on exploration, diplomacy, industry, identity and temporal risk rather than a single queen.
Bilqis is present as a cunning Aza’raan ruler known to disregard laws established when time travel was invented in 2082.
No campaign is obliged to solve the novel’s ancient clue trail.
Her later displacement in 3021 belongs to established chronology, without making it the tabletop interface’s primary quest.
Historical and system reference
Galaxy Era adventures can explore transport, science, factions, artificial environments and legal consequences of time travel. Bilqis is known for being a cunning queen who repeatedly breaches the laws first established in 2082, but her personal archaeological clue hunt belongs to Book Two rather than a tabletop clue ledger.
Next chapter

sections.title: Time Travel and Its Laws
sections.text:
Time travel becomes possible in 2082 CE and prompts legal restrictions.
Before a session involving temporal alteration, the group chooses what violations change: custody of displaced people, evidence admissibility, paradox risk and remembered history.
The system must never treat a lawbreaking act as automatically safe because a famous ruler has done it.
The Bilqis reference is a setting example, not a dedicated clue ledger.
Next chapter

sections.title: Species and Mixed Ancestry
sections.text:
The strict JSON supplies twelve approved original species names and their named variants, while the old MMORPG supplies eighteen race-menu descriptions including several mixed-ancestry groups.
Use one reconciliation table instead of assuming every menu item denotes a separate biological species.
Ampharils are part of Dril’thar ancestry.
Kalus’aans, Kalusogals and Aza’ziras are mixed communities.
The old Azh’raim name is cross-referenced with Azrahai, not silently duplicated.
Historical and system reference
Strict JSON species can be selected as approved. Source-only candidates from the old MMORPG are listed for reconciliation, not enabled by default. Kalus’aans and Kalusogals are historical mixed communities; Ampharils are already part of Dril'thar heritage. Character ancestry should not force one language or one alignment.
Next chapter

sections.title: Settlements and Architecture
sections.text:
Building begins with land rights, access, resources, foundation and utilities.
Spaces require circulation clearance, safety and occupancy limits.
Interior decoration and terrain work have persistent state so the result is more than a temporary combat map.
A home or workshop may alter NPC trust and access to professions.
Tabletop layouts use tiles or coordinates compatible with the MMORPG’s private-dimension grid.
Next chapter

sections.title: Travel and Portal Safety
sections.text:
Designated short-range public portal stops are safer than uncontrolled travel.
Long-range unanchored teleportation risks misarrival, injury and entering hazardous terrain.
In a tabletop game, reveal safe routes and let players plan.
A voyage should have time, supplies and consequences.
The geography dataset must reject passage to Belavadös in any era after the continent has been destroyed.
Historical and system reference
Short-range travel to a designated public transit stop can be safer than unanchored long-distance movement. Track intended destination, anchor status, environmental danger and consequences on failure. Later games must never offer destroyed Belavadös as a valid route.
Next chapter

sections.title: Factions and Communities
sections.text:
Factions have leadership, goals, methods, territories, internal disagreement and material needs.
Players may help a cause without agreeing with every leader.
Track personal relationships separately from public reputation.
The Iron Dominion appears in histories of Belavadös’s destruction, while later organizations reflect migrations and societal change.
A referee should not flatten every culture or people into one set of beliefs.
Next chapter

sections.title: Dialogue and NPC Memory
sections.text:
NPCs remember concrete actions, not only numeric approval.
Each record includes relationships, a recent interaction, unanswered promises, occupation and community ties.
The dialogue generator must not force every speaking character into the author’s exact voice.
A person should be able to decline, negotiate, ask for aid or leave.
Mixed families and multilingual speakers may have different registers without reducing their speech to caricature.
Next chapter

sections.title: Equipment Across Eras
sections.text:
Historical equipment, machinery and Galaxy Era gear belong to separately filtered catalogs.
An item needs an era, source culture, weight, function, maintenance and access restrictions.
A lost artifact may survive a catastrophe through believable custody but should not populate every shop.
Display each effect as a rule and a story consequence.
The digital version uses the same item identifiers so table and screen reports match.
Next chapter

sections.title: Campaign Continuity
sections.text:
Each session records current date and era, party roster, locations, promises, faction changes, crafted work, open travel routes and conflicts.
A change to the Veil or one species name must update the related campaign entry, source glossary and game JSON.
Bilqis is spelled exactly so.
A separate book-series clue record exists for Pix’s investigation, but not as a Galaxy Era gameplay mechanic.
Next chapter

warning: These supporting sources are not the authoritative new 19-letter language model or newer book manuscript. Repeated and old version titles are historical, not an instruction to rename anything.
